Definition: Extent to which the national digital identity system is integrated with the data exchange for identity verification and authentication
Comments: Mauritania has a National Agency for People Registry and Secure Documents (under Ministry of Home Affairs) managing national biometric ID cards, passports, and residence permits. UNDP and MTNIMA piloted e-ID Mauritania in 2024 - an open-source mobile digital identity solution with offline verification capability. The pilot focused on assessing safeguards, privacy, and usability for authenticating government services, private sector and civil society. Integration with government services is being developed. Tech5 and SmartMS contributed technology. Score 3: under development.

Definition: Whether primary laws, acts, or legal instruments exist that establish authority for cross-government data sharing and govern the data exchange system
Comments: Law No. 2017-020 on personal data protection was adopted in 2017 but has NOT yet come into force. Mauritania has ratified the AU Malabo Convention (cybersecurity and personal data). The National Digital Transformation Agenda includes governance and legal framework as an enabler, with plans for data protection enforcement. The National Strategy for Open and Interoperable Data recommends legislative reforms. No dedicated cross-government data sharing law found in effect. Score 2: under development - legislation exists but not in force.

Definition: Whether a detailed implementation roadmap with phases, milestones, and timelines exists for data exchange development
Comments: Mauritania has an implementation roadmap. The Ijraati/Khdamati three-phase roadmap announced Feb 2026: Phase 1 - centralize all procedures on unified platform; Phase 2 - continuous updates and data reliability; Phase 3 - fully digitize most-used procedures and integrate into Khdamati. The National Digital Transformation Agenda 2022-2025 includes phased activities across 4 pillars with specific targets (double internet usage, triple digital economy employment). The WARDIP-Mauritania/World Bank project also has a structured implementation framework. Score 3: yes, roadmap exists.

Definition: Current operational status of the data exchange system
Comments: Mauritania does not have an operational unified data exchange platform. Key digital government platforms include: Khdamati (online services delivery platform, partially operational), Ijraati (directory of 800+ administrative procedures, launched Feb 2026), Digital Road Traffic System (SNTR), and e-ID Mauritania (piloted 2024, developed by UNDP/MTNIMA). These are separate service delivery portals rather than a backend data exchange/interoperability hub. The National Digital Transformation Agenda 2022-2025 called for a government intranet and interoperability framework. National Data Governance Strategy (2022) proposes interoperability standards but implementation is incomplete. Status: planned/early pilots.

Definition: Extent to which the data exchange enables services accessible to all population groups including persons with disabilities, elderly, low literacy
Comments: The e-ID Mauritania pilot explicitly prioritized accessibility by design for low-connectivity areas, offline verification, and multiple identity options on a single phone. UNDP noted the importance of designing for rural populations. However, 44% of population live in rural areas with limited infrastructure and only about 37.4% internet penetration (2025). 56.61% smartphone ownership. The ITU notes Mauritania ranks 165th in EGDI with low online services score. Score 2: partial accessibility.
